claims.text: Uncertainty in LLM outputs increases as the generation temperature setting is increased.
Prompt complexity directly increases output uncertainty, with confusing prompts yielding higher convex hull areas than easy or moderate prompts across models.
GPT-4o achieves lower response uncertainty metrics on confusing prompts at high temperatures compared to GPT-3.5-turbo and Gemini-Pro.
Convex hull area computed over clustered low-dimensional response embeddings quantifies the dispersion and uncertainty of LLM outputs.

evidence.description: For Gemini-Pro on easy prompts, the mean convex hull area increases from 0.3916 at temperature 0.25 to 2.5481 at temperature 1.0; similar monotonic increases are observed across all models.
At a temperature setting of 1.0, GPT-3.5-turbo shows a mean convex hull area of 8.9260 for confusing prompts compared to 2.6992 for easy prompts and 2.2830 for moderate prompts.
At a temperature setting of 1.0 for confusing prompts, GPT-4o has a mean convex hull area of 3.1909, whereas Gemini-Pro reaches 7.7980 and GPT-3.5-turbo reaches 8.9260.
Total convex hull area A(p,t) is defined as the summation of geometric areas of all DBSCAN clusters of 2D PCA-projected BERT response embeddings.

methodologies.name: Convex Hull Geometric Uncertainty Quantification
methodologies.description: A geometric UQ method that converts multiple LLM outputs per prompt into high-dimensional BERT embeddings, projects them to 2D via PCA, clusters them via DBSCAN, and calculates the total convex hull area of the clusters as the uncertainty metric.
conditions: DBSCAN clustering with epsilon=0.25*t*4.0 and min_samples=3

limitations.text: Traditional methods for uncertainty quantification, such as probabilistic models and ensemble techniques, face challenges when applied to complex and high-dimensional LLM-generated outputs.
Most existing uncertainty quantification studies in NLP have limited capabilities and applications, primarily focusing on short text generation.
The evaluation in this study is limited to BERT embeddings, PCA dimensionality reduction, and DBSCAN clustering.

future_work.text: Extend the proposed geometric approach to other types of embedding models and clustering algorithms.
Integrate the convex hull uncertainty metric with other evaluation criteria, such as accuracy and coherence, to provide a comprehensive LLM performance assessment.
